dataset.t: Each dot is **one example described by two features, X**. Nothing says what the groups are yet, so all we see are positions.

labels.t: Now every dot carries a **known label y**. This is the answer the model is allowed to learn from, which is what makes the problem **supervised**.

supervised.t: The model learns a **boundary from labelled examples**, then predicts the label of a **new point** by seeing which side it falls on.

remove-labels.t: Hide y. **Only the features X remain**, exactly as an unsupervised learner sees the data. There is no answer key any more.

unsupervised.t: Group points that are **similar to each other**. The groups are **discovered from X alone**; nobody tells the algorithm what they mean.

compare.t: **Supervised** learning learns to **predict a known target**. **Unsupervised** learning **discovers structure in X**. The difference is whether labels are available.
